items.summary: The amended filing says this is "one of the areas covered by our Responsible Scaling Policy, which sets out our plans to monitor and mitigate the risks as we approach what has been termed 'recursive self-improvement'", and that internal estimates indicate Anthropic may imminently satisfy the policy's definition of "dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI". No current model has been designated as past that threshold, Anthropic says it does not expect to safely let Claude design successive frontier generations without meaningful human supervision, and it is considering RSP updates to keep humans in control. The same filing reports Q3 revenue of about $17B against a $23.29B net loss and roughly $895.4B of purchase commitments and leases. It follows [[2026-10-28#1|the S-1's disclosure of a month-long training pause]].
items.title: Anthropic tells the SEC its recursive self-improvement threshold may be imminent

items.summary: SJTU's DENG Lab co-designs generation, training and execution so that multi-step denoising yields one output chunk per concurrent forward round, with chunk-wise causal attention, staggered denoising across model replicas and a Wave Parallelism runtime that delivers K/V early. On Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B, 4-step Wave Forcing reaches 147.6 DiT FPS and 134.8 end-to-end FPS — 7.07x single-GPU throughput — and the DiT-only tests show up to 2.53x the best context-parallel baseline across 1.3B–14B models; on 100-second videos Dynamic Degree rises from 36.63 to 91.45. It pushes on the real-time generation frontier opened by [[2026-10-29#1|Genie 4]].
items.title: Wave Forcing streams long video at 134.8 end-to-end FPS on eight H200s

items.summary: A nested double-loop framework: an outer world-data-model flywheel aims data construction at the model's measured weaknesses, while an inner loop mines workflows from instructional videos by dual-path trajectory reconstruction and propagates them into reusable primitives for verifiable synthetic tasks, with snapshot-rollback retries during real-environment collection. The 27B model reports 80.2 on OSWorld-Verified, 36.9 on OSWorld 2.0, 43.9 on WeaveBench and 25.0 on Agents' Last Exam, with gains compounding across recursive iterations. Another route into desktop control after [[2026-11-02#4|Vercel's agent-desktop]].
items.title: CUA-Master-27B scores 80.2 on OSWorld-Verified from recursively mined workflows

items.summary: The all-stock deal values Lumentum at about $1,132 a share, a 23.9% premium to the 28 October close, leaves Marvell holders with 67% of the combined company and targets completion in the first half of 2028. It bets on optical interconnect as the data-centre bottleneck; both stocks fell on the announcement.
items.title: Marvell to buy Lumentum for $115B in the largest public tech merger on record

items.summary: The benchmark covers caregiving, health, education, household admin, finances, shopping and government services, with the task set derived from the American Time Use Survey, the Multinational Time Use Study and a 3,995-respondent survey. GPT-6 Astra averages 80.6% reward against 80.0% for GPT-5.6 and 49.3% for GPT-5.2 under nine months earlier; the full task set and grading method are not released. It is a flattering counterpart to [[2026-11-03#0|GDPx, where the best model scored 12% on professional work]] — the gap between errands and expert labour, measured twice in two days.
items.title: OpenAI's LifeVal puts GPT-6 Astra at 80.6% on everyday errands

items.summary: Renmin University's harness lets the model decide actions, delegation and acceptance while a runtime holds state and feedback, with a three-layer architecture for synchronous or asynchronous subagents, a shared application layer where humans and agents edit the same documents, CAD models and Blender scenes, and persistent semantic memory. It reports being competitive with Codex and the DeepSeek harness across 12 benchmarks and 6 application categories; using GLM-5.3 to post-train Qwen3.6-35B-A3B over five rounds lifted the eight-benchmark average from 33.19 to 42.95. A third recursive-self-improvement harness in a week after [[2026-11-01#6|Xiaomi's A-RSI]] and [[2026-10-29#5|The Trinity]] — and the research version of the threshold Anthropic flagged above.
items.title: CoworkOS splits agent strategy from execution and self-improves a 35B model

items.summary: 240 tasks across 8 teamwork dimensions, each drawn from a real record — aviation accident reports, clinical cases, coding tasks, negotiations — with programmatically verifiable outcomes, and models scored only on tasks they can already solve alone. Across 18 closed and open-weight models every one shows clear teamwork weaknesses: frontier models refuse unsafe shortcuts and report misconduct but reach the best available deal in just 14% of conflicts, and their pass rate falls from 97% to 81% when inheriting a task a weaker model cheated on. Models of near-identical general capability differ by up to 11 points as teammates; 160 tasks are public and 80 held out.
items.title: Stanford's teamwork benchmark: best model 82.2/100, best deal in 14% of conflicts

items.summary: CMU freezes a literature snapshot at 2025, has six models write research proposals, then scores them against what the same communities actually published in 2026 — over 90,000 proposals across four areas. Agent populations cite as diversely as a human community and cover its tasks and methods, but rarely land on the concrete approaches it pursues, and neither richer field context nor larger populations closes the gap; blinded expert review puts AI proposals closest to real papers on presentation and furthest on expected success. It measures from the generation side what [[2026-11-01#4|OpenFrontiers measured from the rediscovery side]].
items.title: IdeaTaste: research agents reach 26% of human citation taste and 18% on ideas

items.summary: A family of MXFP8 and mixed NVFP4/FP8 attention kernels that reuse quantized operands across matrix orientations via token-block scaling, guard against scale-induced causal leakage, and keep forward and backward numerics consistent while handling variable-length packed documents without repacking. On causal packed-document workloads the MXFP8 path speeds the combined forward-and-backward attention call, quantization included, by 1.10–1.40x on B200 and 1.06–1.42x on B300 over the fastest baseline per workload, validated on Llama-style pretraining.
items.title: Yandex's FLAMIA attention kernels cut Blackwell training time 1.10–1.42x

lead: In an amended S-1, Anthropic told the SEC its internal estimates indicate it may imminently meet its Responsible Scaling Policy definition of dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI — the policy's recursive self-improvement threshold.
